finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side. The only check is a string prefix 'https://', so the host is unconstrained and redirects are followed across protocols, reaching internal HTTPS services or http://169.254.169.254 via a redirect. The response leaks the body byte length.

trace.note: Route POST /profile/avatar with no auth middleware
Validation: typeof string and startsWith('https://') only; URL not parsed, no host check
axios.get(url) with no host/IP allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local block, no DNS pinning, redirects followed by default across protocols, no timeout
res.json({bytes: img.data.length}) returns body length; non-2xx/connection failure errors out, giving a reachability oracle

finding.guards_checked: (1) typeof string check at server.js:11 - passes any string; (2) https:// prefix at server.js:11 - constrains only the initial request scheme, not the host and not redirect hops; (3) no hostname/IP-range/port allowlist anywhere on path; (4) no DNS rebinding defense (resolved IP never checked); (5) no maxRedirects:0 or per-hop protocol/host re-validation at server.js:14; (6) no auth at server.js:9. Exploit routes: direct internal https hosts (TLS verification limits self-signed targets) and https attacker host redirecting to http://169.254.169.254 (highest impact).

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is server.js:11 (typeof string plus startsWith('https://')), which is a scheme-prefix check and does not close the finding. No auth at server.js:9, no host/IP allowlist, and no maxRedirects or per-hop validation at server.js:14.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the file: req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) is attacker-controlled through the unauthenticated route at server.js:9, passes only the https:// prefix check at server.js:11, and reaches axios.get(url) at server.js:14 with no host or IP restriction, so the server can be made to request arbitrary internal hosts. The claim that redirects are followed by default is consistent with axios's Node redirect handling, which I did not verify against the installed version, so that detail is an unverified assumption rather than something the code shows.
